In February and March 2014, ___E:Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia)___ invaded the ___E:Crimean Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimea)___ , part of ___E:Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine)___ , and then ___E:annexed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexed)___ it. This took place in the relative ___E:power vacuum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_vacuum)___  immediately following the ___E:Revolution of Dignity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity)___ .
It marked the beginning of the ___E:Russo-Ukrainian War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War)___ .

The ___E:events in Kyiv U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity)___ that ___E:ousted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity#Removal_of_Yanukovych)___ Ukrainian president ___E:Viktor Yanukovych U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Yanukovych)___ on 22 February 2014 sparked both pro-Russian and anti-separatism  ___E:demonstrations in Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_2014_Crimean_crisis#February_23)___ .
At the same time, Russian president ___E:Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___ told his security chiefs to begin work on "returning Crimea to Russia".
On 27 February, ___E:Russian special forces without insignia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_green_men_(Russo-Ukrainian_War))___  seized strategic sites across Crimea.
Russia at first denied involvement,  but Putin later admitted that they were Russian troops.

As the armed men ___E:occupied Crimea's parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capture_of_the_Crimean_Parliament)___ , it dismissed the ___E:Crimean government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Ministers_of_Crimea)___ , installed the pro-Russian ___E:Aksyonov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Aksyonov)___ government, and announced a ___E:referendum on Crimea's status U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Crimean_status_referendum)___ .

The referendum was held ___E:under Russian occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_occupation_of_Crimea)___ and, according to the Russian-installed authorities, the result was overwhelmingly in favor of joining Russia.
The next day, 17 March 2014, Crimea's authorities ___E:declared independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_Independence_of_the_Republic_of_Crimea)___ and requested to join Russia.

Russia formally incorporated Crimea on 18 March 2014 as the ___E:Republic of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Crimea_(Russia))___ and ___E:federal city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_cities_of_Russia)___ of ___E:Sevastopol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevastopol)___ .
Following the annexation,  Russia militarized the peninsula and warned against any outside intervention.

Ukraine and ___E:many other countries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_reactions_to_the_annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation)___ condemned the annexation and consider it to be a violation of ___E:international law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law)___ and Russian agreements safeguarding the ___E:territorial integrity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_integrity)___ of Ukraine.

The annexation led to the other members of the ___E:G8 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_of_Eight)___ suspending Russia from the group  and introducing ___E:sanctions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_sanctions_during_the_Ukrainian_crisis)___ .

The ___E:United Nations General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly)___ also rejected the referendum and annexation, adopting ___E:a resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_Resolution_68/262)___ affirming the "territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders",   and referring to the Russian action as a "temporary occupation".

The Russian government opposes the "annexation" label, with Putin defending the referendum as complying with the principle of the ___E:self-determination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination)___ of peoples.

The names of the Crimean annexation vary. In Ukraine, the annexation is known as the temporary occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol by Russia ( ___E:Ukrainian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_language)___ : тимчасова окупація Автономної Республіки Крим і Севастополя Росією , romanized: tymchasova okupatsiia Avtonomnoi Respubliky Krym i Sevastopolia Rosiieiu ), the illegal occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea , the fall of Crimea , and the invasion of Crimea .

In the Russian Federation, it is also known as the accession of Crimea to the Russian Federation ( ___E:Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language)___ : присоединение Крыма к Российской Федерации , romanized: prisoyedineniye Kryma k Rossiyskoy Federatsii ), the return of Crimea ( ___E:Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language)___ : возвращение Крыма , romanized: vozvrashcheniye Kryma ), and the reunification of Crimea .

Crimea was part of the ___E:Crimean Khanate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Khanate)___ from 1441 until it was ___E:annexed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Empire)___ by the ___E:Russian Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire)___ in 1783 by a decree of ___E:Catherine the Great U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_II)___ .

After the downfall of ___E:Russian empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_empire)___ in ___E:1917 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution)___ during the first stages of the ___E:Russian Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Civil_War)___ there were a series of short-lived independent governments ( ___E:Crimean People's Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_People%27s_Republic)___ , ___E:Crimean Regional Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Regional_Government)___ , ___E:Crimean SSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Socialist_Soviet_Republic)___ ).

They were followed by ___E:White Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_movement)___ governments ( ___E:General Command of the Armed Forces of South Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Command_of_the_Armed_Forces_of_South_Russia)___ and later ___E:South Russian Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Russian_Government)___ ).

In October 1921, the Bolshevik ___E:Russian SFSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic)___ gained control of the peninsula and instituted the ___E:Crimean Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic)___ as a member of Russian Federation.
In the following year Crimea joined the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ as a part of Russia (the ___E:RSFSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSFSR)___ ).

After the ___E:Second World War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War)___ and the 1944 ___E:deportation of all of the indigenous Crimean Tatars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportation_of_the_Crimean_Tatars)___ by the Soviet government, the ___E:Crimean ASSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_ASSR)___ was stripped of its autonomy in 1946 and downgraded to the ___E:status U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Oblast)___ of an ___E:oblast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oblasts_of_Russia)___ of the Russian SFSR. In 1954, the Crimean Oblast was ___E:transferred U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_transfer_of_Crimea)___ from the ___E:Russian SFSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_SFSR)___ to the ___E:Ukrainian SSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR)___ by decree of the ___E:Presidium of the Supreme Soviet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidium_of_the_Supreme_Soviet)___ of the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ to commemorate the 300th anniversary of ___E:Ukraine's union with Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Pereyaslav)___ .

In 1989, under ___E:Gorbachev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Gorbachev)___ 's ___E:perestroika U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perestroika)___ ,  the Supreme Soviet declared that the deportation of the ___E:Crimean Tatars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Tatars)___ under ___E:Stalin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin)___ had been illegal  and the mostly ___E:Muslim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ ethnic group was allowed to return to Crimea.

In 1990, the ___E:Soviet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_(council))___ of the Crimean Oblast proposed the restoration of the Crimean ASSR.  The oblast conducted a ___E:referendum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Crimean_sovereignty_referendum)___ in 1991, which asked whether Crimea should be elevated into a signatory of the ___E:New Union Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Union_Treaty)___ (that is, become a ___E:union republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ on its own).
By that time, though, the ___E:dissolution of the Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ was well underway.

The Crimean ASSR was restored for less than a year as part of Ukrainian SSR before the restoration of ___E:Ukrainian independence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Ukrainian_independence_referendum)___ .

Newly independent Ukraine maintained Crimea's ___E:autonomous status U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Republic_of_Crimea)___ ,  while the ___E:Supreme Council of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Council_of_Crimea)___ affirmed the peninsula's "sovereignty" as a part of Ukraine.

The confrontation between the government of Ukraine and Crimea deteriorated between 1992 and 1995. In May 1992 the regional parliament declared an independent "Crimean republic."  In June 1992, the parties reached a compromise, that Crimea would have considerable autonomy but remain part of Ukraine.  ___E:Yuri Meshkov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Meshkov)___ , a leader of the Russian movement was elected President of Crimea in 1994 and his party won a majority in the regional parliamentary elections in the same year. The pro-Russian movement was then weakened by internal disagreements and in March 1995 the Ukrainian government gained the upper hand. The office of the elected President of Crimea was abolished and a loyal head of region was installed instead of Meshkov; the 1992 constitution and a number of local laws were repealed.

According to ___E:Gwendolyn Sasse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwendolyn_Sasse)___ the conflict was defused due to Crimea's multi-ethnic population, fractures within the pro-Russian movement, Kyiv's policy of avoiding escalation and the lack of active support from Russia.

During the 1990s, the serious dispute over control of the ___E:Black Sea Fleet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea_Fleet)___ and Crimean naval facilities, as well as the status of Crimea in whole were ___E:source of tensions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia%E2%80%93Ukraine_relations)___ between Russia and Ukraine.

In 1992, ___E:Vladimir Lukin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Lukin)___ , then chairman of the ___E:Russian Duma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Duma)___ 's Committee on Foreign Affairs, suggested that in order to pressure Ukraine to give up its claim to the Black Sea Fleet, Russia should question Ukrainian control over Crimea.

In 1998 the ___E:Partition Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_Treaty_on_the_Status_and_Conditions_of_the_Black_Sea_Fleet)___ divided the fleet and gave Russia a naval base in Sevastopol, and the ___E:Treaty of Friendship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian%E2%80%93Ukrainian_Friendship_Treaty)___ recognized the inviolability of existing borders.
However, in ___E:2003 Tuzla Island conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Tuzla_Island_conflict)___ issues over maritime border resurfaced.

In September 2008, the ___E:Ukrainian Foreign Minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Ukraine))___ ___E:Volodymyr Ohryzko U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volodymyr_Ohryzko)___ accused Russia of giving ___E:Russian passports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_passport)___ to the population in Crimea, and described it as a "real problem", given Russia's declared policy of military intervention abroad to protect Russian citizens.

On 24 August 2009, ___E:anti-Ukrainian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Ukrainian_sentiment)___ demonstrations were held in Crimea by ethnic Russian residents. ___E:Sergei Tsekov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Tsekov)___ (of the ___E:Russian Bloc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Bloc_(party))___  and then deputy speaker of the ___E:Crimean parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_parliament)___  ) said then that he hoped that Russia would treat Crimea the same way as it had treated ___E:South Ossetia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Ossetia)___ and ___E:Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abkhazia)___ .

Crimea is populated by an ___E:ethnic Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russians_in_Ukraine)___ majority and a minority of both ethnic ___E:Ukrainians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainians)___ and Crimean Tatars, and thus ___E:demographically U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Ukraine)___ possessed one of Ukraine's largest ethnically Russian populations.

As early as in 2010, some analysts already speculated that the Russian government had ___E:irredentist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irredentist)___ plans. ___E:Taras Kuzio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taras_Kuzio)___ said that "Russia has an even more impossible time recognizing Ukraine's sovereignty over the Crimea and the port of ___E:Sevastopol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevastopol)___ – as seen by public opinion in Russia, statements by politicians, including members of the ruling United Russia party, experts and journalists".
In 2011, William Varettoni wrote that "Russia wants to annex Crimea and is merely waiting for the right opportunity, most likely under the pretense of defending Russian brethren abroad".

The ___E:Euromaidan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euromaidan)___ protest movement began in ___E:Kyiv U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv)___ in late November 2013 after President ___E:Viktor Yanukovych U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Yanukovych)___ , of the ___E:Party of Regions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_of_Regions)___ , failed to sign the ___E:Ukraine–European Union Association Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine%E2%80%93European_Union_Association_Agreement)___ .

Yanukovych won  the ___E:2010 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Ukrainian_presidential_election)___ with strong support from voters in the ___E:Autonomous Republic of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_Republic_of_Crimea)___ and ___E:southern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Ukraine)___ and ___E:eastern Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Ukraine)___ .
The Crimean autonomous government strongly supported Yanukovych and condemned the protests, saying they were "threatening political stability in the country".

The ___E:Crimean autonomous parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Council_of_Crimea)___ said that it supported the ___E:government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Azarov_government)___ 's decision to suspend negotiations on the pending association agreement and urged Crimeans to "strengthen friendly ties with Russian regions".
On 4 February 2014, the Presidium of the Supreme Council "promised" to consider holding a referendum on the peninsula's status.

Speaker ___E:Vladimir Klychnikov U:(https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D0%BB%D1%8B%D1%87%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2,_%D0%92%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B8%D0%BC%D0%B8%D1%80_%D0%9D%D0%B8%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B5%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87)___ asked to appeal to the Russian government to "guarantee the preservation of Crimean autonomy".   [importance?] The ___E:Security Service of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Service_of_Ukraine)___ (SBU) responded by opening a ___E:criminal case U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_case)___ to investigate the possible "subversion" of Ukraine's territorial integrity.

On 20 February 2014, during a visit to ___E:Moscow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow)___ , ___E:Chairman of the Supreme Council of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Supreme_Council_of_Crimea)___ ___E:Vladimir Konstantinov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Konstantinov_(politician))___ stated that the ___E:1954 transfer of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_transfer_of_Crimea)___ from the ___E:Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic)___ to the ___E:Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic)___ had been a mistake.
The Euromaidan protests came to a head in late February 2014, and Yanukovych and many of his ministers fled the capital on 22 February.

After his flight, opposition parties and defectors from the Party of Regions put together a parliamentary quorum in the ___E:Verkhovna Rada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verkhovna_Rada)___ (the Ukrainian parliament), and voted on 22 February to remove Yanukovych from his post on the grounds that he was unable to fulfill his duties.    ___E:Arseniy Yatsenyuk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arseniy_Yatsenyuk)___ was appointed by the Rada to serve as the head of a ___E:caretaker government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caretaker_government)___ until new presidential and parliament elections could be held. This ___E:new government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Yatsenyuk_Government)___ was recognised internationally.

Russian government and ___E:propaganda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propaganda_in_Russia)___ have described these events as a " ___E:coup d'état U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ " and have said that the caretaker government was illegitimate,     while researchers consider the subsequent annexation of Crimea to be a true ___E:military coup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ , because the Russian military seized Crimea's parliament and government buildings and instigated the replacement of its government with Russian proxies.

The February 2014 ___E:revolution of Dignity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolution_of_Dignity)___ that ousted Ukrainian president ___E:Viktor Yanukovych U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Yanukovych)___ sparked a political crisis in Crimea, which initially manifested as ___E:demonstrations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_2014_Crimean_crisis#23_February)___ against the new ___E:interim Ukrainian government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Yatsenyuk_Government)___ ,  but rapidly escalated.

In January 2014, the ___E:Sevastopol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevastopol)___ city council had already called for formation of "people's militia" units to "ensure firm defence" of the city from "extremism".

At the end of January 2014, the Russian businessman ___E:Konstantin Malofeyev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantin_Malofeyev)___ travelled with his head of security, former ___E:Federal Security Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Security_Service)___ (FSB) officer ___E:Igor Girkin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Girkin)___ , to Crimea where he met with ___E:Vladimir Konstantinov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Konstantinov_(politician))___ , Chairman of the ___E:Supreme Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Council_of_Crimea)___ , raising the question of whether he would be prepared to take "more drastic measures" to enforce Crimea's autonomy should Kiev descend into complete chaos.

Konstantinov had already met with ___E:Nikolai Patrushev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolai_Patrushev)___ , head of the ___E:Security Council of Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Council_of_Russia)___ , in Moscow in December 2013 where he told Patrushev that if Yanukovych was overthrown, Crimea would be ready to break off and become part of Russia.
At the end of January 2014, Konstantinov met with ___E:Vladislav Surkov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislav_Surkov)___ , Putin's aide in charge of Ukraine.

On February 4, Konstantinov initiated an appeal to Putin to protect the region's autonomy and started preparing a "survey" of Crimeans on what its status should be. Surkov visited Crimea on February 14 where he might have tried to recruit ___E:Crimean prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Crimea)___ ___E:Anatolii Mohyliov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatolii_Mohyliov)___ for the Russian cause.

In response to the rising violence on Maidan, in January local "self-defence" groups started to form. Close to one thousand ___E:Kuban Cossacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuban_Cossacks)___ from the ___E:North Caucasus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Caucasus)___ region joined these units in late February.
They were also reinforced by thousands of Russian soldiers dressed as civilians.
The activities of these groups were closely coordinated with Russian military forces and planned by Russian defence officials.
Igor Girkin was responsible for the operational control of some of the units and their coordination with Russian security officials.
By different counts, close to ten thousand people joined these self-defence groups, but the exact share of locals remains unknown.
On February 20 several buses with Crimean license plates were stopped at a pro-Maidan checkpoint in a town in ___E:Cherkasy oblast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherkasy_oblast)___ .
Their passengers were violently intimidated and some buses were burned.
This incident was subsequently used by Russian propaganda which made unsubstantiated claims that the passengers were killed in gruesome ways.
The ___E:Verkhovna Rada of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verkhovna_Rada_of_Crimea)___ members called for an extraordinary meeting on 21 February.

In response to Russian separatist sentiment, the ___E:Security Service of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Service_of_Ukraine)___ (SBU) said that it would "use severe measures to prevent any action taken against diminishing the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Ukraine". [note 2] [clarification needed] The party with the largest number of seats in the Crimean parliament (80 of 100), the ___E:Party of Regions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_of_Regions)___ of Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych, did not discuss Crimean secession, and were supportive of an agreement between President Yanukovych  and ___E:Euromaidan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euromaidan)___ activists to end the unrest that was struck on the same day in ___E:Kyiv U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv)___ .

Russia was concerned that the new government avowedly committed to closer relations with the West put its strategic positions in Crimea at risk. On 22–23 February [note 3] , Russian president ___E:Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___  convened an all-night meeting with security services chiefs to discuss extrication of the deposed Ukrainian president, Viktor Yanukovych, and at the end of that meeting Putin had remarked that "we must start working on returning Crimea to Russia".

After that ___E:GRU U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GRU_(Russian_Federation))___ and ___E:FSB U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Security_Service)___ began negotiating deals with local sympathizers to ensure that when the operation began there would be well‑armed "local self‑defense groups" on the streets for support.  : 11 On 23 February ___E:pro-Russian demonstrations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_pro-Russian_unrest_in_Ukraine)___ were held in the Crimean city of Sevastopol.

According to political scientist ___E:Daniel Treisman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Treisman)___ , there are doubts about Putin's claim that the decision was made on February 23. According to a source close to the commander of the operation, Russian special forces in the port of Novorossiysk and the Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol had already been put on alert on February 18. On February 20, they were ordered to blockade Ukrainian military bases in Crimea in a "peacekeeping" operation.
Participants in the operation were later presented with a medal for the retaking of Crimea, on which the period of the operation was engraved February 20 to March 18.

Crimean prime minister ___E:Anatolii Mohyliov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatolii_Mohyliov)___ said that his government recognised the new provisional government in Kyiv, and that the Crimean autonomous government would carry out all laws passed by the Ukrainian parliament.

In ___E:Simferopol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simferopol)___ , following a pro-Russian demonstration the previous day where protesters had replaced the Ukrainian flag over the parliament with a Russian flag,  a pro-Euromaidan rally of between 5,000 and 15,000 was held in support of the new government, and demanding the resignation of the Crimean parliament; attendees waved Ukrainian, Tatar, and European Union flags.

Meanwhile, in Sevastopol, thousands protested against the new Ukrainian government, voted to establish a parallel administration, and created civil defence squads with the support of the Russian ___E:Night Wolves U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_Wolves)___ motorcycle club. Protesters waved Russian flags, chanted "Putin is our president!" and said they would refuse to further pay taxes to the Ukrainian state.
Russian military convoys were also alleged to be seen in the area.
In ___E:Kerch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerch)___ , pro-Russian protesters attempted to remove the Ukrainian flag from atop city hall and replace it with the flag of Russia.

Over 200 attended, waving Russian, ___E:orange-and-black St. George U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribbon_of_Saint_George)___ , and the ___E:Russian Unity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Unity)___ party flags.
Mayor Oleh Osadchy attempted to disperse the crowd and police eventually arrived to defend the flag. The mayor said "This is the territory of Ukraine, Crimea.
Here's a flag of Crimea," but was accused of treason and a fight ensued over the flagpole.
On 24 February, more rallied outside the Sevastopol city state administration.

Pro-Russian demonstrators accompanied by neo- ___E:Cossacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cossacks)___ demanded the election of a Russian citizen as mayor and hoisted Russian flags around the city administration; they also handed out leaflets to sign up for a self-defence militia, warning that the " ___E:Blue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union)___ - ___E:Brown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sturmabteilung)___ Europlague is knocking".
